title: A Spinal-Injury Drug Repairs DNA Damage in Alzheimer's
hook: A drug originally developed for spinal cord injury repaired DNA damage and cut brain inflammation in mouse Alzheimer's studies — and it's already cleared a human safety trial.
key_points: KCL-286, a drug originally developed to treat spinal cord injury, showed a new effect in mouse studies of Alzheimer's disease.
It repaired DNA damage in brain cells and reduced inflammation.
Unlike many Alzheimer's drugs that target a single pathway (amyloid or tau), KCL-286 appears to act on multiple disease-related pathways at once.
It has already cleared an initial human safety trial for its original use, which researchers say could let it move faster into Alzheimer's clinical testing.
content_html: Most experimental Alzheimer's drugs narrow in on one target — usually amyloid plaques or tau tangles. A drug developed for an entirely different condition, spinal cord injury, is now showing a broader effect in mouse studies of the disease.
extra_html: As ScienceDaily reports, KCL-286 repaired DNA damage in brain cells and reduced inflammation in mouse Alzheimer's models, while touching multiple disease-related pathways rather than just one. That breadth matters because Alzheimer's has resisted single-target drugs for years. The practical edge here is timing: because KCL-286 already cleared an initial human safety trial for its original use, researchers believe it could move into Alzheimer's-specific clinical testing faster than a drug starting from scratch.

related.title: Scientists May Have Found How Alzheimer's Kills Brain Cells
related.hook: Researchers say they've found a previously overlooked mechanism of brain cell death behind both Alzheimer's and frontotemporal dementia — and it might be possible to interrupt.

related.title: Maybe Plaques Aren't the Whole Story
related.hook: New research suggests Alzheimer's may start not with plaques themselves, but with amyloid beta interfering with tau — the protein that keeps neurons running.

related.title: Keeping Your Brain Healthy
related.hook: No pill prevents dementia, but the habits that protect your heart turn out to protect your brain too.
